The afoxé is an Afro-Brazilian percussion instrument of indefinite pitch, an idiophone. It is built as a hollow container covered with a net bag through which beads or seeds are threaded; when the body is shaken the beads strike the container and make the sound. In ensemble it produces a continuous rhythmic pulse and works with the call-and-response singing of the participants. It is common in the carnival processions of Salvador in Bahia, used by groups formed from Afro-Brazilian communities, playing the ijexá rhythm connected with Candomblé ritual.
Afoxé 為巴西體鳴樂器，構造為中空容器外包網，網中穿珠子或種子。早期以葫蘆與: The afoxé is a Brazilian idiophone, built as a hollow container with a net over it, beads or seeds threaded into the net. Early instruments were made of gourds and coconut seeds; modern ones are mostly mass-produced and made of wood. As for the exact materials of the net, the beads or the seeds, and the kind of wood used for the modern version, the source does not say.
Afoxé可能源自西非舍凱雷，隨被奴役的西非人傳入巴西後，以葫蘆與椰子種子等材料: The afoxé may come from the West African shekere, and after arriving in Brazil with enslaved West Africans it was copied in gourds and coconut seeds. From the late nineteenth to the early twentieth century the Candomblé ritual drumming of Salvador in Bahia entered the public carnival processions and became the ijexá rhythm performance. Filhos de Gandhy, founded in 1949, established the first Salvador afoxé procession, with its music, formation and the white robes and head-cloths of its dress, influenced by the image of Gandhi. In the later twentieth century, as Afro-Brazilian carnival groups in Bahia developed, the ritual colour and the public cultural expression of the afoxé spread further.
共鳴方式獨特，鼓腔內部的碰撞物相互摩擦碰撞，產生連續且細緻的振動共鳴，營造出層次: Its resonance is unusual: the beads inside the body rub and strike one another, producing a continuous, finely detailed vibration that makes a sound of many layers. Beside a rattle drum the afoxé sounds cleaner and stronger; beside a triangle its quality is warmer and softer. The instrument is especially good at making a joyful, excited atmosphere, and it holds an indispensable place in Brazilian samba.
手持樂器，以敲擊方式發聲。手持樂器本體，透過敲擊、搖晃、刮奏或撥彈等方式使樂器本: A hand-held instrument that sounds when struck. Hold the body of the instrument and make it vibrate by striking, shaking, scraping or plucking it. Different parts and different amounts of force give different timbres. In practice, first check that you are holding the instrument correctly, and once the basic way of sounding it is secure, work on rhythm patterns and melodies. Strike the surface with a finger or a drumstick and let the rebound carry the hand back naturally, keeping the wrist relaxed.
阿弗歇鼓具有獨特的沙沙聲和金屬質感，音色明亮而富有穿透力。其聲響由內部的珠子或金: The afoxé has a distinctive rustle and a metallic quality, bright and carrying. Its sound is made by the beads or metal balls inside striking the body, and it has a clear rhythmic, pulse-like character. Its range is relatively fixed, mostly a bright middle-and-high frequency quality with a warm folk colour.
阿弗歇鼓實際用於巴西巴伊亞州薩爾瓦多的嘉年華遊行與非洲裔巴西人打擊樂合奏，常以多: In practice the afoxé is used in the carnival processions of Salvador in Bahia and in Afro-Brazilian percussion ensembles, where several idiophones are often layered to build the ijexá rhythm, linked with call-and-response singing, the pace of the procession and the traditions of Candomblé ritual. In ensemble it provides a continuous rhythmic pulse and the rhythmic frame.
